title: "AI & Education"
subtitle: "Computational thinking in the age of AI"

## Mathematics, Programming, and Artificial Intelligence

The rapid development of generative
artificial intelligence has changed how
students and educators interact with
programming.

AI tools can now generate code, explain
mathematical concepts, and assist with
problem-solving.

This creates new opportunities, but also
raises important questions about how
programming and mathematics should be taught.

## A New Perspective for CTM

When CTM was originally conceived, the
widespread use of generative AI was not
a central consideration.

As these technologies became increasingly
accessible, questions about their role
in mathematics and programming education
became more relevant.

This section explores how computational
thinking can remain an important educational
goal in a changing technological landscape.

## Questions for Mathematics Education

### What Should Students Learn?

If AI can generate working code, which
programming skills remain essential for
students studying mathematics?

How can computational thinking help
students understand, evaluate, and
critically use AI-generated solutions?

### How Can Educators Adapt?

AI-assisted programming introduces new
possibilities for teaching and learning.

It also raises questions about assessment,
independent problem-solving, and how
students demonstrate understanding.

### Using AI Responsibly

AI-generated explanations and code can
contain mistakes.

Students therefore need the mathematical
knowledge and computational understanding
required to evaluate results rather than
accepting them uncritically.

## Experiences and Future Directions

This section will present relevant
experiences, reflections, and educational
resources as they are documented.

The goal is to support thoughtful
discussion about the future of mathematics
and programming education.
